name: Bhai Dayala
role: Sikh leader and companion of Guru Tegh Bahadur
summary: Bhai Dayala (died 1675), a Brahmin Sikh leader of Patna, travelled with Guru Tegh Bahadur to Delhi and, Sikh tradition says, was executed in Chandni Chowk in November 1675.
about: Bhai Dayala, also called Dayal Das, was born into a Brahmin family and became a leader of the Sikh community. According to Wikipedia he headed the sangat at Patna Sahib and oversaw the Guru's representatives in the east. He was close to the family of Guru Tegh Bahadur and sent word of young Gobind Rai's birth to the Guru in Dacca. In July 1675 he left Anandpur with the Guru, Bhai Mati Das and Bhai Sati Das. Sikh tradition says that after refusing to give up his faith he was executed at Chandni Chowk in Delhi; accounts describe boiling water or oil, and say he kept reciting the Japji Sahib. He is remembered with the other two martyrs.
kidSummary: Bhai Dayala was a Sikh leader from Patna who loved the Gurus and cared for the young Gobind Rai. He travelled with Guru Tegh Bahadur to Delhi. Sikhs remember his courage and his steady prayers.

story.title: A Sikh leader in Patna
story.text: Dayala led the Sikh community at Patna Sahib and helped look after Sikh centres in the east.

story.title: News of a baby
story.text: When Gobind Rai was born in Patna, Dayala sent the happy news to Guru Tegh Bahadur, who was then in Dacca.

story.title: Caring for Gobind Rai
story.text: Sikh histories say he helped look after the young Gobind Rai, together with Bhai Kirpal, while the child grew up.

story.title: A trip to Delhi
story.text: In July 1675 he left Anandpur with Guru Tegh Bahadur, Mati Das and Sati Das. The party was arrested on the way and taken to Delhi.

story.title: Standing firm
story.text: Sikh tradition says he refused to give up his faith. Accounts say he kept reciting the Japji Sahib to the end.

story.title: Remembered
story.text: Sikhs remember Dayala together with Mati Das and Sati Das, the three companions who stayed with Guru Tegh Bahadur to the end.

facts.text: He was one of about 25 Sikhs, with Mata Sulakhni, who left Kiratpur with Guru Har Krishan in 1664 to meet Emperor Aurangzeb in Delhi.
He sent word of Gobind Rai's birth to Guru Tegh Bahadur, who received the news in Dacca.
After watching Mati Das die, Dayala is said to have rebuked Aurangzeb and his court, saying cruelty done in the name of religion would bring the empire down.
Accounts differ about the cauldron: his own page and SikhNet describe water heated to boiling, with him reciting Japji Sahib as it heated, while the page on Mati Das says boiling oil.
Wikipedia places Dayala with the Guru at Lakhnaur around 1672, when the Guru's family and young Gobind Rai had come from Patna and were heading for Baba Bakala.
Wikipedia's page on Dayala says he was arrested at Agra, which differs from the other two profiles, where the party is arrested near Ropar. The Agra claim is flagged there as needing a citation.
He appears in Sikh art: a fresco at Gurdwara Baba Bakala, diorama figures at Mehdiana Sahib, and a nineteenth-century painting by Basahatullah.
The Bhai Mati Das Museum in Delhi holds 1984 canvases by Kirpal Singh showing the martyrdoms of Bhai Dayal, Mati Das and Sati Das.
SikhNet connects him to Bhai Balu Ram, who died fighting Mughal forces in Guru Hargobind's first battle.

quiz.q: Which city was Bhai Dayala a Sikh leader in?
quiz.why: He headed the sangat at Patna Sahib.

quiz.q: What did he help do for baby Gobind Rai?
quiz.why: He and Bhai Kirpal helped care for the baby.

quiz.q: Which prayer did he keep reciting?
quiz.why: Sikh accounts say he recited Japji Sahib.

quiz.q: Where was Guru Tegh Bahadur when Dayala sent news of Gobind Rai's birth?
quiz.why: Dayala wrote to the Guru, who was then in Dacca.
